recognize_zh: 周邊血中多顆異常前骨髓細胞，核呈摺疊、雙葉或扭轉狀，細胞質帶細顆粒；另見數顆脆弱、核被拉扯且顆粒散開的破損細胞，符合低顆粒型 APL。
features: Medium to large abnormal promyelocytes, several forming a tight cluster
Folded, bilobed or twisted nuclei with moderately fine chromatin
Moderate cytoplasm with fine purple granulation, some cells relatively hypogranular
Several fragile, disrupted cells with stretched nuclei and dispersed granules (smudged forms)
Background red cells without significant poikilocytosis; platelets not evident in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous abnormal promyelocytes, including a tight cluster of four cells. The cells have moderate amounts of finely granular to hypogranular cytoplasm and folded, bilobed or twisted nuclei. Several fragile cells show disrupted cytoplasm with stretched nuclei and scattered granules. Platelets are not evident in this field. Findings are consistent with the hypogranular (microgranular) variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia; urgent coagulation studies and PML::RARA testing are indicated.

ddx.vs: Promonocytes have grey, vacuolated cytoplasm with sparse fine granules and are strongly nonspecific esterase positive, whereas APL cells show intense MPO and PML::RARA fusion.
CLL smudge cells arise from small mature lymphocytes with no cytoplasmic granules, not from large granular cells with folded nuclei.
Classic APL has dense coarse granules obscuring the nucleus and faggot cells with Auer rod bundles, which are not prominent here.
Mature monocytes are mixed with other normal leukocytes and have abundant grey cytoplasm with lower N:C ratio, without an expanded immature granular population.
